interest: Shows wartime State Department debate on Oregon's land escheat against Japanese owners, and Swiss-relayed inquiries on Japanese law.
overview: File (1942-43): a Peru colonist-monitoring note, and State Department debate on Oregon's escheat of Japanese-owned land, weighing the lapsed 1911 treaty and seeking Japanese property law via Swiss channels.

people.name: Mr. Griffith
people.role: Inquirer on behalf of the State Land Board of Oregon

people.name: W. Franklin
people.role: Official, Special Division, Department of State

people.name: George L. Brandt
people.role: Executive Assistant to the Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet regarding a Peruvian government request for Japanese-speaking agents in connection with the Japanese colony in Peru.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of American Republics
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Peru's Finance Minister requested Japanese-speaking agents to help monitor its Japanese colony.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Japanese Colony in Peru

subfiles.about: Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth's critique of a draft reply to the State Land Board of Oregon regarding Japanese property rights.
subfiles.summary: Hackworth questions citing the lapsed 1911 treaty in a reply to Oregon, since it never granted Japanese land-ownership rights.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Green H. Hackworth on Draft Reply to Oregon State Land Board

subfiles.about: Treaty Division memorandum by W. V. Whittington discussing modifications to a draft letter to Mr. Griffith concerning Japanese land laws and Oregon escheat proceedings.
subfiles.summary: Whittington revises the Oregon reply, noting Japanese law doesn't bind the state's escheat statute, and cuts an admission of ignorance.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from W. V. Whittington to Mr. Barnes Regarding Letter to Mr. Griffith

subfiles.about: Special Division memorandum proposing to obtain Japanese alien real property laws via the Swiss Government.
subfiles.summary: Franklin resists admitting ignorance of Japanese land law, proposing to seek it from Tokyo via Switzerland instead.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Special Division on Japanese Alien Real Property Laws
